title: Two-component ultracold Bose gases with spin-orbit coupling
abstract: These lecture notes provide an introduction to Bose-Einstein condensates with Raman-induced spin-orbit coupling. Owing to the interplay between the peculiar single-particle dispersion, featuring a double-minimum structure, and the two-body interaction, these systems possess a complex phase diagram. Three different quantum phases can be observed, i.e., a stripe, a plane-wave, and a single-minimum phase, each characterized by different broken symmetries. The condensate dynamics is also significantly affected by the spin-orbit coupling, as revealed by the behavior of the Bogoliubov spectrum in infinite systems and the behavior of the discretized collective mode frequencies in trapped configurations, especially close to the phase transitions. In turn, the superfluid and rotational properties are also deeply modified by the coupling between the motional and spin degree of freedom. Finally, a special attention is devoted to the stripe phase and its supersolid character, which can be clearly revealed by the study of its dynamic features.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive theoretical study of two-component Bose-Einstein condensates with spin-orbit coupling. It maps out a complex phase diagram featuring stripe, plane-wave, and single-minimum phases, demonstrating that SOC profoundly modifies superfluidity and rotational dynamics. The research highlights the emergence of supersolid character in the stripe phase through detailed analysis of excitation spectra.
main_problem: The study investigates Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) subjected to Raman-induced spin-orbit coupling (SOC), focusing on the complex phase diagram and dynamic properties arising from the interplay between SOC, single-particle dispersion, and interatomic interactions.
main_result: The system exhibits three distinct quantum phases—stripe, plane-wave, and single-minimum—whose characteristics are deeply modified by SOC. The stripe phase is particularly notable for exhibiting supersolid behavior.
method: Theoretical analysis employs mean-field theory via the Gross-Pitaevskii equation (GPE) and analyzes excitations using Bogoliubov theory to characterize different quantum phases.
model_or_system: The system models two-component ultracold Bose gases realized with Raman coupling, leading to an effective spin-1/2 Hamiltonian. The single-particle dispersion can feature a double-minimum structure depending on the SOC strength ($\Omega_R$).
key_observables: Superfluid density ($ho_s/ho$), moment of inertia ($\Theta$), Bogoliubov excitation frequencies (e.g., breathing mode, spin-dipole mode), and the stripe phase fringe contrast.
important_parameters: SOC strength ($\Omega_R$), detuning ($\delta_R$), Raman coupling ($k_R$), and interaction strengths ($g_{dd}, g_{ss}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field theory (GPE) and utilizes variational Ansätze for the infinite system, which are approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the single-particle energy dispersion ($\varepsilon_{\pm}(p)$) showing double minima, a phase diagram mapping Stripe, Plane-wave, and Single-minimum phases, and plots of collective mode frequencies (e.g., $\omega_B$, $\omega_{SD}$) versus coupling strength.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from introducing the SOC Hamiltonian and the resulting complex phase diagram to analyzing ground state properties using variational methods. It then delves into dynamic measurements like superfluid density, rotational response, and finally examines the distinct phonon modes characterizing each quantum phase.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it explores how engineered synthetic gauge fields (SOC) fundamentally alter the macroscopic quantum phases and collective excitations of ultracold atomic gases, touching upon supersolidity and symmetry breaking in a controllable platform.

Spin-momentum entanglement.note: The new paper explicitly studies two-component BECs with spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which inherently couples internal spin degrees of freedom to external momentum/motion via the SOC term, directly addressing spin-momentum entanglement.
